Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:10:1.hebrew: והכתיב שדך - המיוחד לך, וח"ל לא הקנו לך מן השמים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:10:1.english: But isn’t it written: “Your field”? - That which is designated for you, and outside of Eretz Yisrael was not granted to you from Heaven.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:10:2.hebrew: ההוא למעוטי זרעים - דכלאי הכרם בח"ל, דמשום דאפקיה בלשון זריעה, כתב שדך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:10:2.english: That [serves] to exclude seeds - [Namely,] diverse kinds of the vineyard outside of the Land; for since [the verse] expressed it in the language of sowing, it wrote "your field".

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:11:1.english: Let us ostracize him - For he has transgressed the words of the Scribes.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:11:2.english: Are not understood by you - The laws of diverse kinds are not clear to you.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:12:1.english: Not clear to you - The laws of diverse kinds are not bright and clear to you.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:12:2.hebrew: לא קי"ל כר' יאשיה - בתמיה. וטעמיה דר' יאשיה, לא ידענא מהיכא נפקא ליה דבעינן ב' מיני זרעים וחרצן שלישי; ומפולת יד נפקא ליה (דברים כ״ב:ט׳) מלא תזרע כרמך כלאים — משמע שזריעת הכרם עצמה תהיה בכלאים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:12:2.english: Do we not hold in accordance with Rabbi Yoshiya - [This is stated] as a question. And as for the reason of Rabbi Yoshiya, I do not know from where he derives that we require two kinds of seeds and a grape seed [as] a third; but [the requirement of] a single hand motion he derives from: “You shall not sow your vineyard with diverse kinds” (Deuteronomy 22:9) — implying that the sowing of the vineyard itself must be [done] with diverse kinds.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:13:1.english: Mixing seeds and planting - And not in a vineyard.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:13:2.hebrew: והא אנן תנן כו' - וקס"ד, אפי' כלאי זרעים נמי אסרו ביה, כי היכי דבא"י אסירי מדאורייתא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:13:2.english: But didn’t we learn, etc. - And the initial assumption was that they prohibited even diverse kinds of seeds in it [outside of Eretz Yisrael] as well, just as they are prohibited in Eretz Yisrael by Torah law.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:13:3.hebrew: כלאי זרעים - לא כתיב בהם פן תקדש, דמשדך לא תזרע כלאים נפקו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:13:3.english: Diverse kinds of seeds - “Lest it be sanctified” is not written concerning them, for they are derived from [the verse], “You shall not sow your field with diverse kinds.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:14:1.hebrew: לאו מילתא היא דאמרי - דלא גזרו על כלאי זרעים בח"ל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:14:1.english: The matter that I said is not [so] - [Namely,] that they did not decree against diverse kinds of seeds outside of Eretz Yisrael.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:14:2.english: The garden of the study hall - Which was for the needs of the students, to eat the vegetables in it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:14:3.english: In beds, in beds - [That is,] garden beds, garden beds.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:1:1.hebrew: ניתני או אידי ואידי כו' - דערלה ודכלאים. או ״זה וזה יורד ולוקט״ — דלא אסרו בחוצה לארץ אלא את הזורע או את הלוקט בידים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:1:1.english: Let [the mishna] teach either in both this [case] and that [case], etc. - [That is, the cases] of orla and of diverse kinds [kilayim]. Or [by stating], “In both this [case] and that [case], one may go down and gather” — for outside of the Land [of Israel], [the Sages] only prohibited the one who sows or the one who gathers with [his own] hands.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:2:1.hebrew: ספק לי - לקוט שלא בפני, שיהיה ספק אצלי, ואנא איכול. ובערלה קאי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:2:1.english: Make it doubtful for me - Pick [it] not in my presence, so that it will be doubtful to me, and I will eat [it]. And [the Gemara] is referring to orla.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:2:2.english: The sharp [Sages] of Pumbedita - Eifa and Avimi, the sons of Raḥava of Pumbedita.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:3:1.hebrew: סתום ספיקא ואבד ודאה - כלומר: ספיקו מותר, ודאה אסור. והיתר ספיקא — סתמייהו: להורות בהצנעה, ולא לדרשו ברבים, הואיל ומקילין בה. וכה"ג אמרי' בנדרים (דף כג:) במילתא אחריתי: רב הונא בר חיננא סבר למדרשיה בפירקא, א"ל רבא: תנא סתים לה סתומי, ואת דריש לה בפירקא?! אלמא, סתום — סתום הדבר קאמר. כך השיב רבינו גרשם בר' יהודה זצ"ל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:3:1.english: Conceal its doubt and destroy its certainty - That is to say: its doubt is permitted, and its certainty is forbidden. And [as for] the permission of its doubt, conceal it — to rule [on it] in private, and not to expound it in public, since they are lenient regarding it. And similarly, we say in Nedarim (23b) regarding another matter: Rav Huna bar Ḥinana thought to expound it at the public lecture [pirka]; Rava said to him: “The Tanna concealed it, and you expound it at the public lecture?!” This proves that “conceal” means: keep the matter concealed. So replied Rabbeinu Gershom, son of Rabbi Yehudah, of righteous memory.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:3:2.hebrew: ואבד ודאה - הואיל והן מקילין, אל תתיר להם לספק זה אצל זה, אלא אבד אותם הפירות בידים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:3:2.english: And destroy its definite [produce] - Since they are lenient [regarding it], do not permit them to cast this [produce] into doubt alongside that [produce], but rather destroy those fruits actively [with your hands].

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:3:3.hebrew: והכרז על פירותיהן - של אלו המקילין בה, שטעונין גניזה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:3:3.english: And declare concerning their produce - [The produce] of those who are lenient regarding it, that it requires interment.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:5:1.hebrew: אף החדש - אלמא בערלה כת"ק ס"ל, דקא מוסיף חדש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:5:1.english: Even the new crop - Evidently, regarding orla, he holds like the First Tanna, since he adds [the prohibition of] the new crop.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:5:2.hebrew: ניתני או אידי ואידי כו' - דערלה ודכלאים, או ״זה וזה יורד ולוקט״ — דלא אסרו בחוצה לארץ אלא את הזורע או את הלוקט בידים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:5:2.english: Let [the mishna] teach either "both this and that," etc. - [Regarding the case] of orla and of diverse kinds; or: "Both this [case] and that [case], one may go down and gather" — for they only prohibited outside of Eretz Yisrael one who sows or one who gathers with [his own] hands.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:5:3.hebrew: תני חדש - ולא תתני אף, והכי קאמר: ערלה וכלאים הרי הם כשאר התלויין בארץ, ואין נוהגין בח"ל; אבל חדש נוהג בח"ל, דכתיב בו מושב — כל מקום שאתם יושבים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:5:3.english: Teach: “[The] new crop” - And do not teach “even”; and this is what [Rabbi Eliezer] is saying: Orla and diverse kinds are like the rest of [the mitzvot] dependent on the Land, and they do not apply outside of Eretz Yisrael; but the new crop applies outside of Eretz Yisrael, for regarding it, it is written: “dwelling” — [meaning] wherever you dwell.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:6:1.hebrew: בסוריא מותר - ואי ודאה בח"ל הלכה, היכי מזלזלינן בספיקא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:6:1.english: In Syria it is permitted - And if its definite [prohibition] outside the Land is a halakha [transmitted to Moses from Sinai], how do we treat its doubt so lightly?

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:6:2.english: Thus it was stated - [The] halakha [transmitted] to Moses [from Sinai].

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:7:1.hebrew: לוקין על הכלאים בח"ל דבר תורה - כדיליף לקמיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:7:1.english: [One is] flogged for diverse kinds outside of Eretz Yisrael by Torah law - As [the Gemara] derives below.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:7:2.english: Regarding the grafting of a tree - Grafting one species onto that which is not its own species.

Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:8:1.hebrew: חקתי תשמרו - מדלא כתיב ״ושמרתם את חקתי״, משמע: ״את חקתי אשר מעולם תשמרו״ — מלמד שהזהיר את נח ובניו עליהן. ואלו הן החקים: ״בהמתך לא תרביע, שדך לא תזרע״. ואיזו זריעת כלאים שאני אומר שחקקתים לך כבר? דומיא דבהמה — דבר המסויים, והיינו הרכבה. ומהכא נפקא לן בסנהדרין (דף ס.) דבני נח הוזהרו עליהן. והכא, אתה מוסיף ללמוד מהיקש זה: דומיא דבהמה, אפי' בח"ל — דהא חובת הגוף היא — אף שדך בח"ל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 39a:8:1.english: You shall keep My statutes - Since it is not written: “And you shall keep My statutes,” it implies: “My statutes that are from of old you shall keep” — teaching that He warned Noah and his sons concerning them. And these are the statutes: “You shall not breed your animal [with a diverse kind]; you shall not sow your field [with two kinds of seed].” And which sowing of diverse kinds is [that concerning] which I say that I have already decreed for you? [That which is] similar to [the prohibition regarding] an animal — a distinct entity, and that is grafting [one tree species onto another]. And from here we derive in Sanhedrin (folio 60a) that the descendants of Noah were warned concerning them. And here, you further learn from this juxtaposition: just as [the prohibition regarding] an animal [applies] even outside the Land [of Israel] — for it is a personal obligation — so too, [the prohibition regarding] “your field” [applies] outside the Land.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 39a:10:1.hebrew: ההוא למעוטי זרעים - פירש בקונטרס: זרעים שבכרם, דאין לוקין עליו. אבל אין לפרש כלאי זרעים דקרקע — דבהם לא איצטריך קרא, כיון דחובת קרקע הוא, פשיטא דאין נוהגת אלא בארץ. אבל כלאי זרעים שבכרם איצטריך קרא, אע"ג דחובת קרקע הוא — דס"ד למילפינהו בק"ו דחדש, כיון דאיסורן איסור עולם ואסורין בהנאה; אבל זרעים לא מצי למילף מק"ו דחדש, דהא כלאי זרעים דקרקע אינם אסורים בהנאה, כדאמר לקמן בשמעתין: כלאי זרעים דבארץ לא אסירי בהנאה, בחוצה לארץ לא גזרו בה רבנן:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 39a:10:1.english: "That [verse serves] to exclude seeds" - Rashi explained: Diverse seeds in a vineyard, that one is not flogged for it [outside the Land]. However, one cannot explain [that the exclusion refers to] diverse seeds of the ground, for regarding them a verse was not needed: since it is a land-dependent obligation, it is obvious that it does not apply anywhere other than in the Land [of Israel]. However, for diverse seeds in a vineyard, a verse was needed, even though it is a land-dependent obligation, because one might have thought to derive them via an a fortiori argument from chadash [the new crop], since their prohibition is a permanent prohibition and they are forbidden for benefit; but [ordinary diverse] seeds could not be derived via the a fortiori argument from chadash, for diverse seeds of the ground are not forbidden for benefit, as [the Gemara] says later in our sugya: "Diverse seeds, which in the Land are not forbidden for benefit, outside the Land the Rabbis did not decree regarding them."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 39a:12:1.hebrew: לא קי"ל כרבי יאשיה דאמר עד שיזרע חטה ושעורה וחרצן במפולת יד - פי' בקונט': לא ידעינן מהיכא נפקא ב' מיני זרעים וחרצן שלישי, ומפולת יד נפקא ליה מ"לא תזרע כרמך כלאים", משמע שזריעת הכרם עצמה תהא כלאים, עכ"ל. ונראה דהאי דבעי רבי יאשיה חטה ושעורה וחרצן, היינו דוקא להתחייב משום כלאי הכרם; אבל מכלאי זרעים מתחייב משני מינין, כמו חטה ושעורה, אפי' לרבי יאשיה. ותדע, מדקאמר: "הא כתיב שדך למעוטי כלאי זרעים שבחוצה לארץ", ואי לית ליה לר' יאשיה כלאי זרעים, למה לי "שדך" דמשמע למעוטי ח"ל? אפילו בא"י נמי אינו לוקה! אלא משמע דבכלאי זרעים לא פליג. וכן מוכח בירושלמי, דקאמר התם: "על דעתיה דרבי יאשיה, נאמר: שדך לא תזרע כלאים, לאיזה דבר נאמר: כרמך לא תזרע כלאים?" כלומר: בלא חרצן מיחייב משום כלאים בחטה ושעורה. "חברייא אמרין: להתראה, שאם התרו בו משום שדך ומשום כרמך לוקה שתים", כלומר: כי איכא כרם בהדי כלאים לוקה שתים. ואי איתא דרבי יאשיה לית ליה כלאי זרעים, מאי בעי ליה לרבי יאשיה: "לאיזה דבר נאמר כרמך"? והא אינו לוקה כלל על שדך, כי אם על כלאי כרם! אלא שמע מינה, אית ליה שפיר כלאי זרעים בלא כלאי כרם. וא"ת: אמאי לא בעי רבי יאשיה בכלאי זרעי' אלא שני מינים, ובכלאי הכרם בעי שלשה מינים? וי"ל, דמשמע ליה דקרא ה"ק: "כרמך לא תזרע כלאים", כלומר: בעינן שיהיו כלאים קודם שיבואו בכרם; אבל גבי "שדך", וכלאי זרעים כגון חטה ושעורה, קרוים כלאים להתחייב כשזורען בקרקע, דגוף הקרקע קרוי שדה. ונראה דהלכה כרבי יאשיה. דאף ע"ג דאשכחן כמה משניות דלא כוותיה, כגון: "המעביר עציץ נקוב בכרם" (כלאים פ"ז משנה ח), ו"המסכך גפנו" כו' (שם משנה ה) — מ"מ קי"ל כוותיה, כדאמר בפ' מי שמתו (ברכות דף כב.): "נהוג עלמא כתלתא סבי: כרבי יאשיה בכלאים, וכרבי אלעאי" כו'. ומותר לזרוע תחת הכרם, וגם מותר לזרוע כלאי זרעים בח"ל, כדאמרינן הכא: "רב יוסף מערב ביזרני וזרע", ואף על גב דאמר: "לאו מילתא היא", הא כבר תרצה אביי. ונראה לה"ר שמואל מאיוור"א, דטוב ליזהר שלא לזרוע זרעים סמוך שלשה טפחים מעיקרו של אילן, דנראה כמרכיב זרעים בתוך האילן:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 39a:12:1.english: "Don’t we hold in accordance with Rabbi Yoshiya, who says: Until he sows wheat, and barley, and a grape seed with a single hand motion" - Rashi explained in the Commentary: We do not know from where he derives two species of seeds and a grape seed as a third; and "with a single hand motion" he derives from "You shall not sow your vineyard with diverse seeds" (Deuteronomy 22:9), implying that the sowing of the vineyard itself must be diverse kinds. Thus far are his words. And it appears that this requirement of Rabbi Yoshiya for wheat, barley, and a grape seed is specifically to incur liability on account of diverse kinds in a vineyard; however, for diverse kinds of seeds, one incurs liability for two species, such as wheat and barley, even according to Rabbi Yoshiya. And you may know [this to be so], from that which [the Gemara] said [above, 39a]: "Behold, it is written: '[You shall not sow] your field [with diverse seeds]' (Leviticus 19:19) — to exclude diverse kinds of seeds outside the Land [of Israel]!" For if Rabbi Yoshiya does not hold of [a prohibition of] diverse kinds of seeds [with only two species], why do I need "your field" to imply the exclusion of outside the Land? Even in Eretz Yisrael he would also not be flogged! Rather, it implies that regarding diverse kinds of seeds, he does not disagree [and agrees that two species suffice]. And so is proven in the Yerushalmi, which says there: "According to the opinion of Rabbi Yoshiya, [once] it is stated: 'You shall not sow your field with diverse seeds,' for what purpose is it stated: 'You shall not sow your vineyard with diverse seeds'?" That is to say: without a grape seed, one is [already] liable on account of diverse kinds for [sowing] wheat and barley. "The Colleagues say: For forewarning — so that if they forewarned him on account of 'your field' and on account of 'your vineyard,' he receives two [sets of] lashes." That is to say: when there is a vineyard together with diverse kinds [of seeds], he receives two [sets of lashes]. And if it were so that Rabbi Yoshiya does not hold of [a prohibition of] diverse kinds of seeds [alone], why does [the Yerushalmi] ask for Rabbi Yoshiya: "For what purpose is it stated: 'your vineyard'"? Behold, he would not be flogged at all for "your field," but rather only for diverse kinds in a vineyard! Rather, conclude from this that he indeed holds of diverse kinds of seeds without diverse kinds in a vineyard. And if you should ask: Why does Rabbi Yoshiya require only two species for diverse kinds of seeds, whereas for diverse kinds in a vineyard he requires three species? And it can be said that it implies to him that the verse means as follows: "You shall not sow your vineyard [with] diverse kinds" — that is to say, we require that they already be diverse kinds before they enter the vineyard [i.e., two different seeds plus the grape seed]. But with regard to "your field" and diverse kinds of seeds, [two species] such as wheat and barley are called diverse kinds so as to incur liability when one sows them in the ground, for the ground itself is called a field. And it appears that the halakhah is in accordance with Rabbi Yoshiya. For even though we find several Mishnayot that are not in accordance with his view — such as: "One who transports a perforated flowerpot through a vineyard..." (Kilayim 7:8), and "One who trellises his grapevine..." etc. (ibid., mishnah 5) — nevertheless, we hold in accordance with him, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Mi SheMeito (Berakhot 22a): "The world conducts itself in accordance with three elders: in accordance with Rabbi Yoshiya regarding diverse kinds, and in accordance with Rabbi Ilai..." etc. And [therefore outside of Eretz Yisrael] it is permitted to sow under a vineyard, and it is also permitted to sow diverse kinds of seeds outside the Land, as we say here: "Rav Yosef was mixing seeds and sowing [them]"; and even though he [subsequently] said: "The matter [that I said] is not so," behold, Abaye already resolved it [demonstrating that planting diverse kinds of seeds outside the Land is indeed permitted]. And it appears to the Rabbi, R. Samuel of Évreux, that it is good to be careful not to sow seeds within three handbreadths of the trunk of a tree, for it appears as though one is grafting seeds into the tree.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 39a:5:1.hebrew: תני חדש - וא"ת: אמאי צריך למחוק "אף"? לימא דקאי אכלאים! וי"ל: כיון דאמר רבי אליעזר אין ערלה בח"ל, אין סברא לומר שיהא מחמיר בכלאים יותר מערלה. ועוד אומר ר"י: כיון דכלאים דרבנן וחדש דאורייתא, אין שייך למיתני "אף" אכלאים; ולא פריך אלא אליבא דמ"ד ערלה הלכה למשה מסיני:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 39a:5:1.english: "Teach: 'The new crop'" - And if you say: Why is it necessary to delete [the word] "even"? Let us say that it refers to diverse kinds! And one can say: Since Rabbi Eliezer says that there is no [prohibition of] orla outside of Eretz Yisrael, it is not reasonable to say that he would be more stringent regarding diverse kinds than regarding orla. And furthermore, the Ri says: Since [the prohibition of] diverse kinds is rabbinic and [that of] the new crop is biblical, it is not appropriate to teach "even" regarding diverse kinds; and [the Gemara] raised its objection only according to the one who says [that] orla is a halakha [transmitted] to Moses from Sinai.
